intro: One admission can cover two museum subjects without turning every visit into a guided program. Show what the ticket includes, how a guide is arranged and when a larger group should ask about terms.
customerQuestion: Does our admission cover both museums, and can we arrange a guide?

decisions.label: State the admission coverage
decisions.body: Explain that the published admission covers both the local history museum and Bronko Nagurski museum. Keep the current visit details beside that shared coverage. Visitors should not assume they need two tickets simply because the website presents the collections in separate sections.

decisions.label: Describe the usual visit and guide option
decisions.body: State that visits are mostly self-guided and that a guide is available without an extra charge under the published offer. Explain how groups arrange that help with staff. Free guidance should not imply that a guide is automatically waiting for every unannounced group at every time.

decisions.label: Ask about the group terms
decisions.body: For groups of ten or more, describe the discount as something to request rather than an automatic deduction. Ask for aggregate attendance and the intended visit date. Keep the guide request and group-rate question together for staff review without turning a contact submission into a confirmed group booking.

ownerInputs: Current shared-admission coverage and opening details.
Guide-arrangement process and approved charge wording.
Group threshold and rate-request instructions.
sourceBridge: Koochiching Museums in International Falls combines history and Bronko Nagurski admission, describes a mostly self-guided visit with guide assistance, and asks larger groups to request a discount. Those are separate parts of the visit decision.
limits: Museum staff confirm arrangements, guide availability and rates. An inquiry does not secure a guide or discount. A clearer explanation can preserve the existing contact route without adding a ticketing or group-booking system.

heading: Explain first-come camping before discussing the donation.
intro: A requested nightly donation does not reserve a campsite or extend the permitted stay. Present arrival, length-of-stay and payment information as separate rules, with the age of the published guidance clearly identified.
customerQuestion: Can we hold a site, and how long are we allowed to stay?

decisions.label: Explain how arrival works
decisions.body: The published county park rules describe first-come camping. State that plainly before any contact or donation information so a visitor does not mistake a payment or inquiry for a reservation. Keep the physical park location near Dawson distinct from the mailing address in Madison.

decisions.label: Show the maximum stay
decisions.body: Present the published nine-day maximum beside the stay-planning information. A ten-day plan needs a different discussion rather than an assumption that another nightly donation extends permission. Do not invent an exception process; direct questions to the responsible contact using current owner-approved instructions.

decisions.label: Label the contribution and rule date
decisions.body: Explain the requested nightly donation and the collection boxes at the entrances and bathroom under the published terms. Make clear that the rules were adopted in November 2022 and obtain current confirmation before presenting them as newly verified. The donation explanation should not imply a reserved site or altered stay limit.

ownerInputs: Current confirmation of the November 2022 rules.
Physical arrival directions and separate mailing address.
Approved donation and stay-limit instructions.
sourceBridge: Lac qui Parle County’s park information near Dawson combines first-come camping, a nine-day limit and requested donations, with rules dated November 2022. Those details need distinct explanations rather than one payment-led action.
limits: The county confirms current rules and access. A donation does not establish a booking or exception. This proposed content must retain the dated-source qualification until the owner verifies current terms; no automated camping reservation is implied.

heading: Compare what the lighthouse ticket lets you enter.
intro: Grounds access, interior admission and guided experiences cover different parts of a lighthouse visit. Show the spaces included and distinguish the guided portion from what visitors explore afterward.
customerQuestion: Does this ticket include the lighthouse interior, and when can we enter it?

decisions.label: Separate grounds from interiors
decisions.body: Explain that the published grounds pass does not include the lighthouse or keeper’s-house interiors. Compare it with general admission using current approved coverage. A dramatic exterior photograph should not make every ticket look like the same full-site experience.

decisions.label: Explain the guided and self-guided parts
decisions.body: Conquering the Cliff has an outdoor guided portion, while its ticket allows self-guided interior visits afterward. State that sequence clearly. The visitor should not expect the guide to take them through every interior simply because interior admission is part of the overall ticket.

decisions.label: Check the season-specific tour
decisions.body: Describe the Keeper’s Tour with its published maximum of ten and current seasonal timing. Do not carry a summer before-opening arrangement into winter without confirmation. Keep dates and ticket links attached to the exact experience so a visitor can compare the actual offered time and coverage.

ownerInputs: Current grounds and interior admission coverage.
Guided and later self-guided visit sequence.
Keeper’s Tour seasonal schedule and attendance limit.
sourceBridge: Split Rock Lighthouse in Two Harbors distinguishes grounds-only access, general admission and guided experiences whose interiors may follow the guided portion. Seasonal timing adds another real ticket difference.
limits: The operator confirms current access, times and availability. A ticket description is not an access assessment for an individual visitor, and a schedule does not hold a place. This content can clarify existing ticket choices without creating a new sales system.

heading: Ask how you may copy the archive material before visiting.
intro: Free research-room access does not permit every copying method or publication use. Explain the available research help, the archive’s device rules and the separate discussion needed for a usable image.
customerQuestion: Can I make my own copy, or should I ask staff for an image?

decisions.label: Choose the research route
decisions.body: Describe free room use separately from staff research offered as available and the obituary service. Explain how to ask about holdings and staff help before a visit. A general research contact should not imply unlimited staff search time or guarantee that the requested record is present.

decisions.label: State the copying restrictions
decisions.body: The public example prohibits personal scanners and archive photography. Put those rules beside visit preparation and explain the approved way to request copies. A visitor should not travel expecting to digitize material with their own equipment because a general museum policy appears to allow ordinary photographs elsewhere.

decisions.label: Discuss the intended image use
decisions.body: Explain that digital resolution varies and that publication or commercial use needs a separate price and permission discussion. Ask for the item reference and intended output. Receiving an image should not be presented as automatically receiving the rights or resolution needed for every possible publication.

ownerInputs: Current room, staff-research and obituary arrangements.
Approved copying methods and device restrictions.
Image-resolution, publication and permission contact.
sourceBridge: Lake of the Woods County Historical Society in Baudette separates room use from staff services, restricts personal copying devices and distinguishes image availability from publication arrangements. Those limits affect visit preparation and output choice.
limits: Staff confirm holdings, copy methods and use terms. A digital file does not establish reproduction permission.

heading: Make the rentable building and public park access clear.
intro: A nature-center rental does not necessarily include every farm building or exclusive use of the park. Explain the actual space, the lead time for the event size and the fee category before an organizer starts a request.
customerQuestion: Which building can we rent, and will the park still be open to others?

decisions.label: Name the rentable space
decisions.body: Identify the Education Building as the rentable building in the public example. Explain that other farm buildings serve storage or classes rather than presenting them as alternative rental rooms. Use labeled photographs so the attractive wider site does not imply a broader space offer.

decisions.label: Match the lead time to the event
decisions.body: Show the ordinary two-week lead time separately from the three months required for large events. Ask for approximate attendance and the intended activity so staff can assess the appropriate arrangement. Do not let a single generic advance-booking note hide the larger-event requirement.

decisions.label: Explain access and the fee category
decisions.body: State that the park remains open to the public during a rental. Also explain that a nonprofit charging admission does not receive the nonprofit rate under the published terms. Keep those conditions beside the rental description so organizational status or a room booking does not imply private park access or automatic pricing.

ownerInputs: Current Education Building rental scope.
Ordinary and large-event lead-time definitions.
Public-access and nonprofit-rate terms.
sourceBridge: Ney Nature Center in Henderson distinguishes one rentable building, different event lead times, continuing public park access and a nonprofit-rate condition. Those points define the actual offer before an event request.
limits: Staff confirm event suitability, availability and rates. A request does not reserve other buildings or grant exclusive use of the park. This content clarifies the existing rental process without supplying event approval or new booking functionality.

heading: Compare cabins and campsites with their own season and pet terms.
intro: A year-round cabin and a seasonal campsite should not inherit the same dates, utilities or pet charges. Help guests choose the type of stay first and keep the current rate year visible.
customerQuestion: Are we booking a cabin or a campsite, and which conditions belong to that choice?

decisions.label: Separate the stay types and seasons
decisions.body: Describe year-round cabins independently from the camping season. Show which dates and contacts apply to each, including the city-office route for availability or longer stays. A combined accommodation heading should not suggest that every campsite remains open because cabins are available in winter.

decisions.label: Identify the campsite utilities
decisions.body: The published Lakeside sites have full hookups while other sites have water and electricity. Keep that distinction with the selected camping location. Do not let a general amenities list imply that sewer connections are available on every pitch or that cabin facilities describe campsite equipment.

decisions.label: Apply the correct rates and pet terms
decisions.body: Label the published rates as 2026 until a newer approved schedule is supplied. Explain the cabin pet charge separately from the no-extra-pet-fee camping terms. A guest should not carry either rule across accommodation types simply because the property descriptions appear on the same page.

ownerInputs: Current cabin and campground seasons.
Location-specific hookup information.
Approved rate year, pet terms and city-office contact.
sourceBridge: City of Hendricks information distinguishes year-round cabins from camping, Lakeside full hookups from other sites and separate cabin versus camping pet terms. The choice of accommodation changes several practical conditions.
limits: The city confirms availability, current rates and permitted stays. Retained 2026 rates should not be presented as a later season’s prices without approval. The website can clarify existing options without promising a live accommodation inventory.

heading: Remove the unavailable room from the current rental choice.
intro: A temporary exhibition can take a meeting room out of rental use while another space remains available. Make the current choice clear and keep the unavailable room’s old equipment list from becoming a description of the alternative.
customerQuestion: Which museum space can we actually ask to rent now?

decisions.label: Show the temporary room status
decisions.body: The October 15, 2026 notice says the conference room is unavailable because of a temporary exhibit. Put that status before a rental action and label retained room details as inactive information. Do not let an old capacity or equipment section override the newer availability notice.

decisions.label: Describe the alternative on its own terms
decisions.body: The ice cream shop remains a rental option in the published notice. Give it its own approved description, layout and equipment information rather than borrowing the conference room’s attributes. If those details are not yet confirmed, direct the organizer to staff instead of filling the gap from a nearby room description.

decisions.label: Prepare the request and future update
decisions.body: Explain the requirement for at least a week’s notice and an agreement before the event. Ask for the preferred date and intended use of the available space. Assign an owner to revise the room status after the temporary exhibition; do not invent a reopening date from the word temporary.

ownerInputs: Current confirmation of the conference-room closure.
Accurate ice-cream-shop rental facts.
Agreement, notice period and status-update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Lyon County Museum in Marshall announced a temporary conference-room closure while retaining ice-cream-shop rentals. The notice changes the current offer and prevents the old room’s details being reused for another space.
limits: Museum staff confirm space availability and rental terms. A request does not book the alternative or establish when the conference room returns. This content correction can preserve the existing agreement process without creating a new booking system.

heading: Explain what the online campground search actually covers.
intro: A booking search may show only part of a campground’s inventory. Tell guests which sites are represented and what to do when the search has no result, without implying that all sites are sold out or that an office call guarantees a place.
customerQuestion: Does this search cover every campsite, and what should I do if nothing appears?

decisions.label: Describe the online subset
decisions.body: The public example describes 104 water-and-electric sites overall but introduces eight sites for online daily, weekly and monthly booking. Show those counts with their different meanings. Do not label the online search as the entire campground unless the operator confirms that its scope has changed.

decisions.label: Give a useful no-result step
decisions.body: Explain how guests enter arrival and departure dates, then offer the office contact when no suitable result appears. A failed search of the online subset does not establish that all 104 sites are occupied. Equally, the contact step should not promise that staff will find another site.

decisions.label: Keep season and rate information current
decisions.body: Distinguish in-season and off-season contacts where the published arrangements differ. Label any 2027 rate information by year rather than applying it to the current period. Let staff confirm the site type, stay length and applicable terms through the established route.

ownerInputs: Current total inventory and online-bookable subset.
Search instructions and no-result office contact.
Seasonal contacts and clearly dated rates.
sourceBridge: Marshall County’s Florian Park distinguishes its full 104-site inventory from eight newly online-bookable sites. That makes the search boundary and office fallback important parts of the visitor’s decision.
limits: The park confirms availability and booking terms. A no-result screen is evidence only about that search, and an office inquiry is not a reservation. Clarifying the boundary does not imply a new inventory integration or guarantee additional capacity.

heading: Give a recording contribution its own first conversation.
intro: Someone offering a family recording needs different help from someone searching for an existing photograph. A clear service introduction can separate finding information, contributing a story and asking for a readable transcript.
customerQuestion: Can you assess this recording, and what would happen to it?

decisions.label: Start with the purpose
decisions.body: Offer clear choices for an archive search, an oral-history contribution, a transcript or a venue inquiry. For a recording, ask whether the person wants to contribute it, obtain a text copy or discuss both. One choice should not silently authorize the other.

decisions.label: Ask for a description first
decisions.body: A few sentences about the recording, its format and approximate length can help staff decide how to respond. Explain the approved next exchange before inviting the file itself. A person should not have to complete a genealogy questionnaire merely to ask about a recording.

decisions.label: Explain acceptance and permission
decisions.body: Show who assesses the material and how the organization discusses handling, the requested output and permission. Keep those steps with the contribution instructions. If the existing contact route works, clearer descriptions may be sufficient; upload or transcription features need their own assessment.

ownerInputs: Accepted services and the staff contact for each.
Useful recording details and the approved exchange process.
Current acceptance, permission and transcript-output instructions.
sourceBridge: Dassel Area Historical Society describes archive searches, oral-history contributions and conversion of recordings to text. Those different purposes make it a useful example of task-based inquiry choices.
limits: A request for a transcript does not donate the recording or grant permission to publish its contents. Staff decides what can be accepted and supplied. The proposed page explains that process; it does not promise automatic transcription or unrestricted use.

heading: Keep each activity’s limit with the school visit.
intro: A field trip may accommodate the whole class while an optional lesson accepts a smaller group. Show the core visit and additions separately so teachers can prepare a request that staff can turn into a workable day.
customerQuestion: Can our whole class take part in the activities we want?

decisions.label: Identify the core experience
decisions.body: State the core program, intended grades, duration and capacity together. The public example describes a two-hour-fifteen-minute experience with capacity for 125 per time slot. Make clear which facts belong to that core offer before presenting optional lessons or crafts.

decisions.label: Keep additions specific
decisions.body: Attach each lesson’s own participant limit and duration. In this example, optional museum lessons take 30 minutes and accept at most 30 students. A 60-student request therefore needs staff planning rather than an assumption that the core capacity also covers one lesson. Keep craft grade guidance visible too.

decisions.label: Prepare the complete day
decisions.body: Ask for the total students, grades, selected additions and proposed date. Include requested lunch or shopping stops in the information staff receives. A core-only duration should not remain the stated length after those stops are added. Use the existing field-trip request route where it supports these details.

ownerInputs: Current program descriptions, grades and activity-specific limits.
Approved durations and lunch or shopping arrangements.
The request route and person confirming the itinerary.
sourceBridge: Mille Lacs Indian Museum’s field-trip guidance distinguishes core capacity from optional lessons and crafts, making the selected activity—not the largest published number—the useful basis for this comparison.
limits: The example does not prescribe a rotation plan or promise acceptance for a particular class. Museum staff designs and confirms the visit. Automatic scheduling, capacity enforcement and changes to booking tools require separate scope.

heading: Show the right payment sequence for each archive request.
intro: Staff research and a commercial image order can follow different payment steps at the same archive. Put the sequence beside the chosen service so a requester knows what to send first and when payment is expected.
customerQuestion: Should I pay now, request an invoice or complete a permission form first?

decisions.label: Choose the research route
decisions.body: Separate an on-site visit from asking staff to investigate remotely. Explain any call-ahead instructions and copy charges for visitors. For remote work, ask for the historical question and useful identifying details without treating free museum admission as free staff research.

decisions.label: Prepare the research invoice
decisions.body: The public example says research requires no prepayment and a bill accompanies the findings. A requester wanting a card invoice should say so in the initial inquiry and supply the required mailing address. Keep these instructions together so the preference is not discovered only after work is sent.

decisions.label: Give image orders their own sequence
decisions.body: A commercial-image request begins with the intended use and the organization’s permission form. Its reproduction and commercial-use fees are paid before release. Show that sequence separately from research billing, and link the maintained instructions rather than repeating exact fees across several pages.

ownerInputs: Current visiting, remote-research and copy-service instructions.
Approved billing steps and card-invoice request wording.
The image permission form and payment/release contact.
sourceBridge: Morrison County Historical Society publishes research billed with findings alongside a different permission and pre-release payment process for commercial images. That contrast supports two clear service paths.
limits: Staff confirms charges, research scope and permissions. A request does not guarantee a successful search, and paying for an image does not replace its permission process. Payment collection, archive downloads and rights-management tools are separate features.

heading: Arrange trail equipment, a hosted tour and transport separately.
intro: A visitor may want to explore independently, join a volunteer-led outing or arrange a journey to the site. Give each option its own preparation and contact instructions so one request does not appear to confirm everything.
customerQuestion: Who confirms the trail experience and how we get there?

decisions.label: Explain independent equipment use
decisions.body: Describe the equipment reservation and staff introduction together. The public example offers powered track chairs for two hours, with a tutorial before use; reservations are preferred and walk-ins are welcome. Keep those terms beside that option rather than borrowing the hosted tour’s notice period.

decisions.label: Describe the hosted outing
decisions.body: Golf-cart tours in the example require at least two weeks’ notice and depend on trail conditions and volunteer drivers. Ask which experience the visitor wants and provide a practical question route. A submitted request should identify what staff still needs to confirm, without implying that a driver is already assigned.

decisions.label: Keep the journey distinct
decisions.body: Name the transport provider and the period when its offer applies. The cited SMART Transit arrangement is described for June through August. Explain how to contact that provider separately, then give written arrival instructions for the center. A trail reservation should not read as a transit-seat confirmation.

ownerInputs: Current equipment terms, tutorial and reservation contact.
Tour notice, season, conditions and confirmation process.
Approved transit wording, provider contact and arrival guidance.
sourceBridge: Jay C. Hormel Nature Center separates track-chair use, advance golf-cart tours and a seasonal SMART Transit offer. Its different providers and notice periods show why each arrangement needs its own explanation.
limits: Staff and the transport provider confirm individual arrangements. The website does not decide which equipment suits a person or ask for diagnoses in a general inquiry. Equipment allocation, transport coordination and booking integrations require separate assessment.

heading: Say which parts of the visit are still available.
intro: Suspending a guided activity does not necessarily close the whole destination. A current notice should name the affected experience while leaving accurate information about other visits, buildings and the shop easy to find.
customerQuestion: What can we still see and do on the day we plan to visit?

decisions.label: Describe each visit format
decisions.body: Explain what a guide provides and what visitors can experience independently. Use an actual example, such as a turntable demonstration, to show why the distinction matters. An open park should not imply that a guided demonstration or every interior is included in a self-guided visit.

decisions.label: Attach restrictions to their subject
decisions.body: Put a guided-tour suspension beside the guided offer, and a building closure beside that building. Keep unaffected options visible. Where physical-access information differs between buildings, describe each one using the operator’s approved wording rather than transferring one exception to the entire site.

decisions.label: Keep the notice current
decisions.body: Show the applicable period and give unresolved questions a staff contact. Agree who updates temporary restrictions and checks related descriptions, photographs and action links. A focused edit may handle the comparison and notice; a broader project can connect exhibits, seasonal preparation and group inquiries.

ownerInputs: Current guided and self-guided inclusions.
Approved building restrictions and access descriptions.
Seasonal dates, notice owner and staff contact.
sourceBridge: End-O-Line Railroad Park and Museum describes staff-dependent guided tours that may stop in extreme weather while self-guided visits and the shop continue. Its building-specific restrictions make partial-status notices useful.
limits: The operator decides what can operate and when restrictions change. A page update does not make a weather or access determination. Automated operational feeds, ticket behavior and weather decisions need separate assessment; this work explains the approved current position.

heading: Ask about each intended use of an archive image.
intro: Obtaining a digital copy and receiving permission to publish it are different steps. An image inquiry should describe the material and where it will appear, including any later use that differs from the original request.
customerQuestion: Does permission for our website also cover a printed display?

decisions.label: Identify the requested material
decisions.body: Let a visitor distinguish research help from a reproduction request. Ask for the item reference or the details staff needs to locate it. Keep the copying or file-delivery service clear without presenting its charge as a complete answer to a publication request.

decisions.label: Name the intended uses
decisions.body: Ask whether the image is for personal study, a website, print or another purpose. A business planning both a website image and a printed display should identify both. This gives the reviewer a concrete question and avoids treating one downloaded file as permission for every future use.

decisions.label: Show the permission contact
decisions.body: Place the organization’s approval route beside reuse guidance. In this example, the Research Coordinator considers each individual and separate use. Explain what happens after review using approved wording, and direct a changed or additional use back to that process rather than extending earlier permission automatically.

ownerInputs: Service categories and useful image-identification details.
Current permission instructions and reviewing contact.
Approved examples of use requests and communicated conditions.
sourceBridge: Nicollet County Historical Society distinguishes reproduction services from permission for each separate use of its material. The website-and-printed-display example turns that distinction into a useful first question.
limits: The organization and appropriate professionals decide permissions. The proposed page does not interpret copyright or promise that a reproduction charge grants publication rights. Image licensing, payments, downloads and rights-management software require separate assessment.

heading: Choose the visit purpose before relying on opening hours.
intro: A gallery visit, research appointment and evening photography session may share a campus but follow different arrangements. Organize the page around what the visitor wants to do, then show the relevant hours, appointment or permission instructions.
customerQuestion: Can I simply arrive, or does this visit need an advance arrangement?

decisions.label: Separate everyday visits from appointments
decisions.body: Give gallery and shop hours their own clear labels. Keep research and artifact-donation appointment instructions beside those activities, even when someone hopes to arrive during general opening hours. One campus admission description should not silently remove another service’s preparation requirement.

decisions.label: Explain access outside normal hours
decisions.body: A photographer considering an evening session needs the current pass or permit route before planning around the grounds. Ask about the intended time and use, then identify who confirms the arrangement. A photograph of an outdoor space is not itself an invitation to unrestricted after-hours access.

decisions.label: Connect the purpose to the next action
decisions.body: Use a short comparison linking each activity to its actual contact or preparation page. A focused edit may be enough if those routes already work. If information is scattered across campus descriptions, bring the activity introductions and their conditions together without inventing a combined permission process.

ownerInputs: Current gallery, shop and grounds information.
Research, donation and after-hours appointment instructions.
Approved pass/permit wording and responsible update contacts.
sourceBridge: History Center of Olmsted County publishes gallery hours separately from appointment-only research and donations, and describes advance passes or photographers permits for grounds access outside normal hours.
limits: Staff confirms access and the actual visit arrangement. A general admission price or inquiry receipt does not grant an appointment or photography permission. Permit processing, payments and automated access decisions need separate scope; this page would explain the existing approved routes.

heading: Give an unsuccessful archive search a useful next step.
intro: An online index may represent only part of a collection. Explain its coverage and give researchers two ways to continue: ask about a likely entry or send a bounded question when the search has not found an answer.
customerQuestion: Does no online match mean there is nothing else to research?

decisions.label: Describe the search’s coverage
decisions.body: Name the resource and explain what its published coverage includes. Distinguish an index reference from the underlying record. A missing result should not become a claim that the whole archive contains nothing relevant, particularly when only a fraction of the collection is represented online.

decisions.label: Retain a useful match
decisions.body: When a researcher finds a likely entry, tell them which name, date and reference to keep for staff. Connect that information to the existing lookup route. Avoid sending them into a general inquiry that loses the very detail needed to identify the material.

decisions.label: Bound an unanswered question
decisions.body: For a broader inquiry, ask for the person, place, approximate period and what has already been searched. Staff can then explain the suitable service and any charges. The page should offer a next conversation without turning every failed search into a paid order or promising a successful investigation.

ownerInputs: Current online-resource descriptions and coverage limits.
Useful reference fields for a specific lookup.
Research-service distinctions, contact and charging instructions.
sourceBridge: Otter Tail County Historical Society says its online resources represent only a fraction of its collection and offers lookup and broader research services. That makes the search-result handoff an important content decision.
limits: Staff determines availability, effort and service terms. An index entry does not guarantee a copy, and no match does not establish that a record is absent. Digitization, searchable archive development, payment collection and request tracking are separate work from clarifying these existing routes.

heading: Check the hours for every part of a combined visit.
intro: A café, museum and shop at one destination may open at different times. Help visitors check the activities they want to combine before choosing when to travel or asking staff about a group outing.
customerQuestion: Can we eat, visit the exhibits and browse the shop on the same day?

decisions.label: Give each activity its own hours
decisions.body: The public Sunday schedule lists the Little Mermaid Café from 9 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., while museum exhibits and the antique/gift shop open at noon and close at 3 p.m. A 10 a.m. breakfast therefore does not include immediate exhibit access. Noon to 2:30 p.m. is the listed overlap for those activities, subject to current opening confirmation.

decisions.label: Keep seasonal choices visible
decisions.body: The thrift store lists Saturday hours of 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. Its season is inconsistent across public pages: the homepage says mid-May to mid-October, while the shop page says May through September. Ask the owner to reconcile the season before publishing one current range; neither description makes the thrift store a Sunday option.

decisions.label: Prepare a combined group request
decisions.body: Ask which activities the group wants, the day and approximate attendance. The museum homepage requests contact for groups of twelve or more; the café page asks groups of ten or more to call ahead. Keep each threshold with its service and pass the meal and exhibit intentions to the appropriate contacts without implying that one request reserves both.

ownerInputs: Current hours and seasons for each activity.
The group threshold and actual planning contact.
Approved combined-visit arrangements and update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Pine County Historical Society’s public pages, checked October 27, 2026, distinguish Sunday museum and café hours, Saturday-only thrift shopping and different group-contact thresholds. Their conflicting thrift-store seasons remain a question for the owner.
limits: Staff confirms group arrangements and any exceptions. The proposed page should not extend opening hours, invent a package or treat a meal request as a confirmed museum tour. Meal reservations, ticketing changes and synchronized calendars require separate assessment; clear hours and preparation may be enough.

heading: Explain archive copying rules before the visit.
intro: Someone preparing to research in person needs to know which equipment can be brought and how copies are obtained. Put those practical instructions beside visit preparation, then explain the separate process for a photograph intended for publication.
customerQuestion: May I bring a laptop or scanner, and how do I request a copy?

decisions.label: Prepare the working visit
decisions.body: State the current equipment policy and workspace limitations in plain language. The public example permits laptops but notes limited space, while personal scanners and archive photography are not allowed. A visitor should see these distinctions before packing equipment and making the journey.

decisions.label: Show how staff makes copies
decisions.body: Ask for the material reference and the reproduction needed, then link the organization’s existing staff-copy instructions. Explain any research-time or copying service separately. Access to a collection should not be described as access to a self-service scanning or download system that the organization does not offer.

decisions.label: Keep the intended use attached
decisions.body: Distinguish personal research from proposed publication or another non-personal use. This example requires a signed photographic agreement before release for non-personal use. Show the responsible contact and approved sequence, so an initial research visit does not appear to settle later permission questions.

ownerInputs: Current equipment policy and workspace guidance.
Staff-copy process, service descriptions and contact.
Photographic agreement and authorized release instructions.
sourceBridge: Pipestone County Historical Society distinguishes permitted laptop use, staff-made copies and restrictions on personal scanning, then provides a separate photographic-agreement step. These facts belong together in practical visit preparation.
limits: The organization interprets its rules and makes permission decisions. Paying for research time or entering the archive does not authorize publication. Uploads, image licensing, payments and collection databases need separate scope.

heading: Give each adult the right school-trip instructions.
intro: Teachers, drivers and accompanying parents may arrive and pay in different ways. A shareable preparation page can turn a confirmed school visit into a clear set of responsibilities without making everyone decode the same long instructions.
customerQuestion: What do the organizer, bus driver and parents each need to do?

decisions.label: Prepare the organizer’s totals
decisions.body: Keep students, teachers, support staff and parents distinct in the attendance information. Include the actual confirmation process and the instructions for packing lunches by class. These categories help staff prepare the visit without asking the website to collect unnecessary individual participant records.

decisions.label: Explain who pays whom
decisions.body: The public example invoices the school after the trip; parents pay the school and payment is not taken at the site. Put that instruction where accompanying parents can find it. A general admission link should not send them toward an on-site purchase that does not match the school arrangement.

decisions.label: Give vehicle-specific directions
decisions.body: Name the approved bus entrance and distinguish bus parking from parent parking. In this example, drivers need the Cleveland Avenue entrance rather than only a general postal address. Link the directions from the teacher’s shareable page and identify who maintains them when arrival arrangements change.

ownerInputs: Current count categories and class-lunch preparation.
School invoicing and parent-payment instructions.
Approved entrances, parking directions and update contact.
sourceBridge: Ramsey County Historical Society’s Gibbs Farm guidance separates participant counts, school billing, class lunches and arrival by vehicle role. It supports a practical organizer/driver/parent page rather than one undifferentiated visit checklist.
limits: These instructions support a visit already arranged through the organization’s process. A planning-form receipt does not confirm a booking or change payment collection. Booking automation, participant records, payments and automated messages need separate assessment; staff approves the actual trip details.

heading: Match the stay length and full party to the campground’s rules.
intro: An extended stay may use a different site category from a weekend visit. Show that choice with the included guest allowance, then explain how to ask about extra guests or another night.
customerQuestion: Which site category fits our stay, and does our whole party need approval?

decisions.label: Choose the eligible stay category
decisions.body: The public example confines weekly and monthly stays to its seasonal section and directs availability questions to staff. Connect the intended duration to that section before showing site amenities. A monthly guest should not choose any pitch simply because it has water and electricity.

decisions.label: Describe everyone in the party
decisions.body: Explain the published long-term allowance of two adults and two children under 18. Additional guests require office preapproval and additional fees. Keep the full party in the inquiry rather than treating another adult as automatically included within a general family description.

decisions.label: Explain later changes and current status
decisions.body: Separate weekend advance reservations from adding another night, which requires space and re-registration by noon under the published terms. Keep campground status distinct from the suspended tubing and kayaking notice. Neither that river-activity closure nor the camping policy page establishes whether camping is currently open; the owner must supply its current status.

ownerInputs: Current stay categories, party allowances and guest fees.
Weekend reservation and extra-night instructions.
Dated campground and river-activity status with update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Voyageur’s View near Red Lake Falls distinguishes seasonal-section extended stays, approved additional guests and conditional extra nights. Its separate river-activity suspension makes service-specific status equally important.
limits: This is a dated policy example, not an invitation to book an open campground. Staff confirm current operation, availability and guest approval. A request does not extend an existing stay; booking changes or live inventory require separate scope.

heading: Allow enough time beyond the last-admission cutoff.
intro: Being allowed to enter shortly before closing does not mean there is time for the visit a family wants. Explain the recommended duration, then identify which buildings and nearby destinations need separate planning.
customerQuestion: When should we arrive, and which places are included in this visit?

decisions.label: Compare entry time with visit time
decisions.body: The museum recommends at least 45 minutes excluding gift-store browsing, but last admission is 30 minutes before closing. Show both figures with current hours. A family arriving at the cutoff should not read it as the recommended arrival time for the suggested full visit.

decisions.label: Explain the available museum spaces
decisions.body: Describe the day-valid admission and the buildings currently offered. Keep Masters Store & Hall visibly marked as not ready for tours, and identify the upstairs area’s access limitation using current approved wording. A building photograph should not imply that every pictured interior is available to visit.

decisions.label: Plan the dugout as a separate stop
decisions.body: Give the dugout site outside town its own directions and current visit or admission information. Do not imply that the museum ticket covers it. An approved map can distinguish the museum and separate destination without estimating travel time or presenting a suggested outing as a confirmed itinerary.

ownerInputs: Current hours, entry cutoff and duration guidance.
Building availability, day-entry and access terms.
Separate dugout directions and visit information.
sourceBridge: Laura Ingalls Wilder Museum in Walnut Grove distinguishes a 45-minute recommended visit from its 30-minute last-entry cutoff, and separates unfinished or limited-access spaces from the dugout destination outside town.
limits: The operators confirm current access and admission arrangements. Suggested duration is planning guidance, not a guarantee of a complete visit. Clear maps and content can support the existing visit routes without adding combined ticketing or an automated trip planner.

heading: State whether the yearbook is a gift or should come back.
intro: A collection can welcome both permanent donations and temporary offers for scanning. Explain the inventory notation first, then preserve the contributor’s intended arrangement before staff discuss handling an original.
customerQuestion: Does the collection need this school and year, and can I have the original returned?

decisions.label: Explain the inventory counts
decisions.body: The public example aims for three copies of each school and year and uses parenthetical copy counts. An unmarked year means one research copy, not a missing yearbook. Show a short annotated example and the date checked so contributors can understand the list without assuming that every listed year still needs another copy.

decisions.label: Keep the contribution choice explicit
decisions.body: Ask for the school, year and whether the person proposes a permanent donation or scanning with return. Carry that preference into the staff conversation. Do not ask someone to send an original before staff confirm the current need and agree the applicable handling arrangements.

decisions.label: Separate volunteer work from item offers
decisions.body: Describe indexing searchable PDFs as a different volunteer inquiry. Give it its own clear contact purpose while retaining the staff-approved contribution route. The availability of a scan or copy count should not be presented as permission to publish the yearbook’s contents or as a promise that every offer will be accepted.

ownerInputs: Current inventory, notation and update responsibility.
Donation and scan-and-return handling arrangements.
Volunteer indexing tasks and appropriate contacts.
sourceBridge: Renville County Historical Society’s yearbook page describes copy-count notation, a three-copy goal, donations, scanning with return and volunteer indexing. The original owner’s intention is the important distinction in this collection example.
limits: Staff confirm needs, acceptance and handling before an item is sent. A scanning inquiry is not a permanent gift or publication permission. File uploads, shipping, digitization and rights management require separate assessment from clearer collection content.

heading: Give the museum and historic house separate visit instructions.
intro: Two properties run by one society can have different visit formats, notice requirements and group limits. Keep the chosen site attached to its address and contact so visitors do not treat museum hours as a house appointment.
customerQuestion: Are we visiting the museum, the house or both, and what does each stop require?

decisions.label: Compare the experiences
decisions.body: Describe the self-guided museum separately from the appointment visit to Alexander Faribault House. Use approved descriptions and photographs to help visitors decide which interests them. A shared organization name should not make the two properties look like adjoining rooms covered by one walk-in visit.

decisions.label: Keep the limit and notice with the house
decisions.body: State the house’s published maximum of five people and distinguish its appointment notice from the museum’s group notice. A party of six should see the house limit before planning the trip. Use the owner’s current notice periods rather than inventing one rule for both properties.

decisions.label: Attach the correct address to each stop
decisions.body: Show the museum at 1814 NW 2nd Avenue and the house at 12 NE 1st Avenue with their own arrival instructions. If visitors want both, explain who confirms the separate arrangements. A suggested two-stop outing should not become an implied reservation or a guaranteed combined itinerary.

ownerInputs: Current site descriptions, addresses and visit formats.
Separate notice periods, group limits and arrival details.
Contact responsible for a proposed combined visit.
sourceBridge: Rice County Historical Society distinguishes a self-guided museum from the appointment-only Alexander Faribault House, with separate addresses and a house limit of five. Those facts make each stop its own planning decision.
limits: Staff confirm the appointments and any combined arrangements. The website does not infer transport time or availability between stops. Clear property cards may be sufficient; itinerary tools or combined booking need a separately agreed scope.

heading: Put boarding-pass collection before the tour departure.
intro: A reserved wildlife tour may require an earlier check-in at a specific park entrance. Explain the experience first, then keep the collection deadline and correct directions together so visitors arrive ready to join it.
customerQuestion: Where do we collect our boarding passes, and how early must we be there?

decisions.label: Describe the prairie experience
decisions.body: Use the operator’s current tour description and participation requirements before presenting the reservation action. State that bison sightings are not guaranteed. A wildlife photograph can illustrate the setting without promising that every trip will encounter the same animals or conditions.

decisions.label: Show the earlier collection deadline
decisions.body: Reserved passengers collect boarding passes at the ranger station at least 20 minutes before departure. For an illustrative 11 a.m. tour, that means collection by 10:40 a.m. Label departure and collection separately so the ticket time does not become the visitor’s target arrival time.

decisions.label: Send each party to the right route
decisions.body: Identify the park office on 161st Street/County Road 20 as check-in and explain that GPS can lead to the wrong entrance. Keep school or adult-group arrangements separate from buying individual tickets. Give the current group, access and weather-change contacts so visitors can confirm their actual instructions before travel.

ownerInputs: Current tour description and participation guidance.
Boarding-pass deadline and approved entrance map.
Group-arrangement and operational-update contacts.
sourceBridge: Minnesota DNR’s Blue Mounds prairie and bison tour combines a 20-minute boarding-pass deadline with a specific ranger-station entrance and a warning about GPS directions. Those details make arrival more specific than a general park map.
limits: The operator confirms tour status, participation and group arrangements. A reservation does not guarantee a wildlife sighting. The content can clarify the existing sequence without providing safety approval, automatic weather updates or a new ticket system.

heading: Choose an exhibit visit or a working-factory tour.
intro: An open visitor center does not mean a factory tour is running. Separate the activities, then show the production check and group preparation that apply specifically to the factory experience.
customerQuestion: Can we visit the exhibits, tour the factory or arrange both?

decisions.label: Give each activity its own schedule
decisions.body: Show Experience Center visiting hours separately from factory tours, which depend on scheduled production. A Saturday exhibit visit should not imply a factory departure simply because the center is open. Keep current descriptions and contact details with the activity they actually cover.

decisions.label: Call ahead for the factory tour
decisions.body: Ask visitors to name the factory tour when checking the current production schedule. Explain the separate arrangements for groups of 15 or more. An illustrative group of 16 needs that group conversation rather than assuming that the ordinary call-ahead instruction alone settles the visit.

decisions.label: Confirm factory preparation
decisions.body: Present the operator-approved footwear, age and carried-equipment or camera restrictions with the factory plan. Do not invent missing requirements or apply factory restrictions indiscriminately to every exhibit visitor. Explain how staff confirm the arranged visit and where the party checks current instructions before traveling.

ownerInputs: Separate activity descriptions and current schedules.
Factory contact and group of 15 or more arrangement process.
Approved participant preparation and confirmation wording.
sourceBridge: Polaris in Roseau separates Experience Center hours from production-dependent factory tours, identifies groups of 15 or more and publishes factory-specific preparation. The desired activity is therefore the first useful choice.
limits: Polaris confirms production access, group arrangements and all factory requirements. A call or website inquiry does not establish permission to enter. This content can preserve the existing process without adding a tour scheduler or assessing participant eligibility.

heading: Help teachers choose the history trunk by the lesson.
intro: A kit title alone may not tell a teacher whether its activity fits the class. Compare grade range, learning purpose and classroom task before asking for dates, then explain how borrowing is confirmed.
customerQuestion: Which trunk supports this class’s lesson, and what should I prepare?

decisions.label: Compare the learning choices
decisions.body: Pieces of the Past introduces daily life through chores, games and school for ages 4–7. What’s for Dinner serves grades 1–2 with food, farm and store activities. Then and Now uses maps, photographs and objects for grades 3–5, while the Minnesota River and Fur Trade program is for grades 6–8. Put the actual audience beside the topic so a title alone does not decide the lesson.

decisions.label: Preview the classroom work
decisions.body: Then and Now asks pupils to compare earlier towns with the present through discussion, games and skits. Its third- and fourth-grade plans last 45 minutes; the fifth-grade plan lasts 50. The program can be led by a society educator or facilitated from the trunk by the borrower. Keep grade, duration and delivery format together when a teacher asks about preparation.

decisions.label: Request the selected trunk
decisions.body: Ask for grade, lesson purpose and intended dates through the existing reservation route. Make clear that the form is followed by staff confirmation. Keep the selected trunk and relevant version visible in that request; student names and class rosters are unnecessary for this initial planning conversation.

ownerInputs: Current trunks, grade ranges and learning objectives.
Approved activity previews, contents and teacher preparation.
Borrowing terms and staff confirmation process.
sourceBridge: Scott County Historical Society’s trunk overview and Then and Now details, checked October 27, 2026, supply these grade/topic choices and different program lengths. Its request form starts a staff-confirmed borrowing conversation.
limits: The society confirms suitability, availability and borrowing arrangements. A request does not reserve the trunk. Clear comparisons and previews may be enough; inventory, scheduling or participant-data tools would require separate assessment.

heading: Show the separate rooms and combined space accurately.
intro: A divided meeting room can support different event arrangements, but its combined capacity should not be applied to either half. Help organizers describe the layout and kitchen use they need before staff review the request.
customerQuestion: Do we need one room or both, and what does the kitchen arrangement include?

decisions.label: Compare the room arrangements
decisions.body: Show Oak Savanna and Woodland separately and together using approved layouts. The published capacity of 50 applies to the combined space. Do not assign that figure to one room or derive an approval from attendance alone; the event format and actual arrangement also need staff review.

decisions.label: Describe equipment and refreshments
decisions.body: Explain the kitchen facilities and what their use includes under current terms. Ask whether the event needs a separate discussion area, refreshments or particular equipment. A workshop organizer can then describe how both rooms or the divider would be used rather than requesting the largest capacity by default.

decisions.label: Explain eligibility and confirmation
decisions.body: Identify the eligible user categories and ask the requesting organization to describe its event. State that the rental request is not confirmed until the specified email is received. A submission receipt should not look like that approval unless it actually carries the venue’s confirmed arrangement.

ownerInputs: Approved separate and combined room layouts and capacities.
Kitchen facilities, equipment and inclusion terms.
Eligible user categories and actual confirmation process.
sourceBridge: Sherburne History Center distinguishes separately usable Oak Savanna and Woodland rooms from their combined 50-person arrangement and requires email confirmation. The room configuration changes the practical request.
limits: The venue confirms suitability, availability and the rental. The website does not approve a layout from headcount or guarantee kitchen use. Clear diagrams and wording can support the existing review process without introducing an automatic booking or capacity calculator.

heading: Keep the overnight permission call after the paper permit is removed.
intro: Year-round park access does not authorize an overnight stay or make every facility available in winter. Separate day use from camping and explain the permission step that still applies during the camping season.
customerQuestion: Can we camp on this date, and what permission do we need first?

decisions.label: Choose day use or an overnight stay
decisions.body: Describe the park’s year-round access separately from its overnight offer. A visitor planning a walk needs current day-use information, while a camping plan also needs the permitted season and approval instructions. An Open year round heading should not make those two activities appear to follow the same rules.

decisions.label: Show the seasonal facilities
decisions.body: The published camping and portable-toilet season runs from May 1 through November 1, and the park has no electricity. Put those facts beside the intended date and stay type. A December day visitor should not expect seasonal toilets, and an in-season camper should see the absence of electricity before making plans.

decisions.label: Retain the permission requirement
decisions.body: Explain that paper camping permits are no longer required but visitors must still call the Sheriff’s Office for overnight permission. Keep the current contact next to that statement. Removing an obsolete form link must not remove the call or make a July camping plan look approved simply because it falls within the season.

ownerInputs: Current day-use, camping and facility dates.
Approved no-electricity and permission wording.
Sheriff’s Office contact and update responsibility.
sourceBridge: Sibley County’s High Island Creek Park guidance distinguishes year-round entry from seasonal camping and toilets, while retaining an overnight permission call after ending paper permits. That change is the central planning detail.
limits: The county grants permission and confirms current arrangements. Website wording, an in-season date or a contact message does not authorize a stay. Clear content can preserve the existing permission route without creating a camping reservation system.

heading: Describe the rooms visitors reach and the rooms shown on video.
intro: A broad accessibility label cannot explain a historic property with different entrances and stair-only floors. Show the actual route and any video alternative so visitors can decide which information to discuss with staff.
customerQuestion: Which rooms will we enter physically, and how do we reach each floor?

decisions.label: Map the stair-free entrances
decisions.body: The public example describes stair-free access to the main and lower floors through separate entrances. Label those entrances with verified photographs or a route diagram. Do not suggest an internal lift or connection that the operator has not described, and keep current path or slope information attached to the relevant approach.

decisions.label: Identify the video substitution
decisions.body: Explain that upper floors are reached by stairs and that the Limited Mobility Tour includes a tablet video of the second floor. Keep the rooms visited physically separate from those represented on the tablet. The alternative should be described accurately rather than presented as identical access to every interior.

decisions.label: Offer a practical staff conversation
decisions.body: Show how to arrange the relevant tour and where to ask questions about the route. Ask what information would help the visitor plan, without requesting a diagnosis or medical records. Staff-approved descriptions and actual alternatives should guide the discussion before the party chooses or purchases a visit.

ownerInputs: Verified floor access and separate-entrance images.
Exact tour coverage and video alternative.
Current arrangement instructions and access-information contact.
sourceBridge: Glensheen distinguishes main- and lower-floor stair-free entrances from upper-floor stairs and describes a second-floor tablet video within its Limited Mobility Tour. The physical route and represented rooms are different parts of the experience.
limits: The operator confirms current routes and arrangements; visitors can assess their own needs using that information. This content does not certify accessibility or invent an alternative route. Broader tour or booking changes need separate scope.

heading: Put the capacity beside the meeting layout it describes.
intro: The largest published room capacity may not fit a discussion or classroom arrangement. Compare the layouts first, then ask about breakout space and equipment that change the event’s needs or cost.
customerQuestion: How will people work in the room, and does that layout fit our attendance?

decisions.label: Compare the working arrangements
decisions.body: Use approved classroom, U-shaped and lecture illustrations with their own capacities. The public example lists 25 for the U-shaped arrangement and 75 for lecture seating. A 30-person U-shaped request should not be presented as fitting simply because the room can hold 75 in another configuration.

decisions.label: Describe the breakout requirement
decisions.body: Explain the partition option and keep the separate Board Room distinct from the large-room layouts. Ask whether the event needs a separate discussion area and how it will be used. A divider request should stay visible with the main meeting plan so staff can assess the whole arrangement.

decisions.label: Identify equipment and extra charges
decisions.body: State which items are included and which kitchen or presentation options cost extra. Let the organizer name the projector, refreshments and other needs in the existing inquiry. Do not silently treat a requested item as supplied or included, and leave the final suitability and setup discussion to staff.

ownerInputs: Current layout capacities and approved diagrams.
Partition, Board Room and setup arrangements.
Equipment inventory, kitchen terms and additional charges.
sourceBridge: Stearns History Museum distinguishes layout-specific capacities, a partition and separate Board Room, with additional-cost kitchen and presentation options. Its 25-seat U-shape and 75-seat lecture figures demonstrate why headcount alone is insufficient.
limits: The venue confirms the actual arrangement, availability and charges. A layout illustration is a planning reference, not an approval. Clear comparisons can improve the existing inquiry without introducing a capacity calculator or automatic room booking.

heading: Separate the short museum tour from the organized full-day itinerary.
intro: A visit to one historical site does not automatically include a whole day of activities or lunch. Show the available time, the sites involved and the organization that confirms each kind of visit.
customerQuestion: Do we want a short tour, a suggested day out or the arranged full-day program?

decisions.label: Describe the society’s tours
decisions.body: The published group tours run from 45 minutes to two hours and require three weeks’ notice. Distinguish the History Center, Village of Yesteryear and Orphanage Museum with their own descriptions and arrival details. Ask which sites interest the group and how much time is available before presenting a combined plan.

decisions.label: Name the full-day organizer
decisions.body: Identify Step Back in Time as a separate full-day itinerary arranged through the chamber. Keep its contact and confirmed inclusions with that offer. A request for a short History Center tour should not look like a request for the chamber’s complete day.

decisions.label: Label meals and suggestions accurately
decisions.body: Explain that lunch is included in the named chamber itinerary, while downtown lunch in a sample day plan is a suggestion. Keep travel and meal responsibilities clear using current approved arrangements. An illustrative schedule can help visitors compare possibilities without becoming a confirmed itinerary or implying that suggested stops are booked.

ownerInputs: Current site descriptions, tour lengths and notice period.
Chamber itinerary contact and approved inclusions.
Arrival, meal and transfer responsibilities for each offer.
sourceBridge: Steele County Historical Society distinguishes short group tours from the chamber-arranged Step Back in Time day with lunch. Its separate sample visit plan suggests downtown lunch, which is a different level of commitment.
limits: Each responsible organization confirms its arrangements and inclusions. A suggested outing or inquiry does not book multiple sites or meals. Clear comparisons can preserve current contacts; combined booking or itinerary tools require separate assessment.

heading: Carry the index reference into the research conversation.
intro: Finding an entry online does not provide the underlying record or permission to handle it. Show what visitors can browse themselves and where staff retrieval or copying is the next step.
customerQuestion: What can I consult independently, and what should I ask staff to retrieve?

decisions.label: Use the finding tools
decisions.body: Explain the online cemetery and newspaper indexes and show an approved example of a useful reference. Ask researchers to retain the topic and identifying details. An index match can help begin a search without proving that the original is available, complete or downloadable.

decisions.label: Distinguish browsing from retrieval
decisions.body: Describe the shelves and card catalog visitors may use, then name the collection materials or database searches that require staff assistance. Keep those handling boundaries near research preparation. A general invitation to explore the collection should not imply unrestricted access to every original.

decisions.label: Discuss copies and the visit
decisions.body: Explain the staff route for copies or scans and the current instructions for arranging an onsite session. Let the researcher bring a reference and intended question into that discussion. A contact acknowledgement should not promise that material has been retrieved or that a copy can be supplied in the requested form.

ownerInputs: Current indexes and approved reference examples.
Freely browsable and staff-retrieved material categories.
Copying, staff availability and visit instructions.
sourceBridge: Stevens County Historical Society distinguishes public shelves and a card catalog from staff retrieval, database assistance and copying, with online indexes that help start the search.
limits: Staff confirm holdings, access and copies. An index result is a finding reference, not a document or permission. New catalog or file-delivery systems require separate scope.

heading: Keep the serviced tent site visible in the comparison.
intro: Sites within one camping category may have different amenities, and a longer stay may need a different booking contact. Connect both choices before the guest follows the reservation instructions.
customerQuestion: Which tent site has the services we need, and where do we arrange a longer stay?

decisions.label: Show the tent-site exception
decisions.body: The public example lists tent sites 1 through 3 without water or electricity, while tent site 4 has both. Put those identifiers beside the amenities and on the approved map. A single Tent sites label should not hide the serviced option or imply the same utilities across all four.

decisions.label: Explain the reservation requirement
decisions.body: State that all sites require reservations. Keep the chosen site identifier understandable when a visitor moves from the map to the existing booking instructions. An unserviced site should not appear to be first come simply because it lacks hookups or has a simpler description.

decisions.label: Use the longer-stay contact
decisions.body: For stays longer than seven days, direct visitors to the city office to check availability. An eight-night tent stay needing electricity therefore raises both the site 4 choice and the office-contact step. Do not imply that the ordinary online booking route settles an extended stay or guarantees that particular site.

ownerInputs: Current site identifiers, map and amenities.
All-site reservation instructions and booking labels.
Over-seven-day contact and applicable stay terms.
sourceBridge: Appleton Municipal Campground distinguishes three unserviced tent sites from serviced site 4 and directs stays over seven days to the city office. The exception and duration both affect the next step.
limits: The city confirms availability and the stay arrangement. A map choice is not a reservation. Clear site comparison can support the existing provider; changes to inventory, booking rules or payment require separate assessment.

heading: Keep water-status questions separate from campsite allocation.
intro: A reply about facilities does not reserve a first-come campsite. Explain the arrival rule, obtain a dated water update and keep the published electrical-use limit visible for parties bringing several campers.
customerQuestion: What facilities can we expect, and does contacting the county hold a site?

decisions.label: State the arrival rule
decisions.body: Explain that the park operates first come, first served and does not allow reservations. Place that rule beside the Highway Department contact. Asking about facilities should not imply a campsite hold, and a group should not assume a reply secures adjoining sites.

decisions.label: Replace uncertainty with a dated update
decisions.body: The public page carries a planned October water-shutoff notice without a year. Ask the owner to confirm current water status and its applicable date before publishing a current claim. If it remains unresolved, direct visitors to the department rather than reusing the old notice as confirmation for the intended visit.

decisions.label: Explain the stated sharing limit
decisions.body: The published instruction limits an electrical pedestal to two plugged-in campers. Keep that wording with multi-camper preparation; three campers should not be shown sharing one pedestal. Use the owner-approved map and facility instructions without deriving electrical specifications from a symbol or designing a connection arrangement.

ownerInputs: Current no-reservation and arrival wording.
Confirmed water status, year and update owner.
Approved pedestal limit, map and department contact.
sourceBridge: Traverse County Park separates first-come camping, an undated seasonal water notice and a two-camper pedestal limit. The missing notice year is a specific reason to seek current operator information.
limits: The county confirms facility conditions. Contact does not allocate sites or approve electrical arrangements. This content clarifies published instructions; it does not design connections, create reservations or treat an old seasonal notice as current evidence.

heading: Show whether the ticket reserves an Eagle Program seat.
intro: General admission and a reserved program experience secure different things. Explain the ticket inclusions before purchase and give visitors wanting two named experiences the staff-contact route for that combination.
customerQuestion: Does this option reserve the program we want, or only admit us to the center?

decisions.label: Compare the admission choices
decisions.body: Describe general admission separately from the options that reserve an Eagle Program seat. Use the exact current experience and ticket names found in the provider. A visitor should understand what has been secured without assuming that entering the center automatically includes a reserved place in every program.

decisions.label: Explain walk-in uncertainty
decisions.body: State that walk-in program seats are not guaranteed under the published instructions. Keep this information beside general entry, where it affects the decision. A visitor can then consider the intended experience before following the ticket link rather than learning the distinction after arrival.

decisions.label: Route the combined experience to staff
decisions.body: Visitors wanting both an Eagle Program and Behind the Scenes are instructed to call. Show that route clearly and explain the information staff need to discuss the combination. Do not encourage someone to assemble two separate online products and assume they form a workable, confirmed itinerary.

ownerInputs: Current ticket names and exact inclusions.
Walk-in seating terms and experience descriptions.
Combined-visit contact and approved booking links.
sourceBridge: The National Eagle Center distinguishes general entry from a reserved Eagle Program seat and directs visitors combining that program with Behind the Scenes to call. The selected ticket therefore matters beyond admission alone.
limits: The center confirms availability and combined arrangements. A contact message does not reserve either experience. A clear comparison can preserve current sales routes; ticket-provider changes or automatic itinerary combinations require separate scope.

heading: Label pavilion electricity separately from RV hookups.
intro: Electrical service for an event does not establish that overnight campers have hookups. Show which use each facility supports before an organizer arranges a gathering with RV visitors.
customerQuestion: Can we request power for the pavilion, and what facilities will the RV guests have?

decisions.label: Explain the pavilion arrangement
decisions.body: Describe the park and pavilion reservation route with current owner-approved terms. State that electricity must be requested when reserving. Keep the event’s intended equipment or power question with that request rather than assuming every pavilion booking automatically includes the same electrical arrangement.

decisions.label: Describe RV facilities independently
decisions.body: The public example allows RV campers to use the parking area and states that no hookups are available. Put that statement beside overnight information. A photograph of a powered pavilion or a general Electricity available icon should not imply that RV guests can connect to campsite services.

decisions.label: Keep both plans visible
decisions.body: For a reunion or similar gathering, let the organizer describe the pavilion event and ask separately about overnight preparation. Use an approved map to show the relevant places without suggesting that one reservation confirms the other arrangement. Direct practical facility questions to the responsible park contact.

ownerInputs: Current pavilion reservation and electricity-request terms.
Approved RV parking and no-hookup description.
Event and overnight contacts, map and preparation details.
sourceBridge: Wadena County’s Old Wadena Park information allows electricity to be requested with a pavilion reservation but separately describes RV parking without hookups. The same amenity word therefore needs a specific use and location.
limits: The park confirms the event arrangement and overnight instructions. This content does not approve an electrical setup or imply an RV connection. A focused label and contact change may be sufficient; broader reservation or facility tools need separate scope.

heading: Identify the photograph and intended output before requesting a quote.
intro: A web image may help a researcher recognize a photograph without being suitable for publication. Show the identifier and format limits, then explain the information staff need to assess a reproduction request.
customerQuestion: Can this particular image be supplied at the size and quality we need?

decisions.label: Retain the exact reference
decisions.body: Ask for the accession number and catalog location of the image. Use an approved example to show where those details appear. The public collection’s web images are reference quality, so a visible thumbnail should not be treated as the finished file for printing or publication.

decisions.label: Check the output limitation
decisions.body: State that LU-prefixed images are not available at high resolution under the published guidance. Place that exception beside the identifier information before the quote step. Ask for the desired size or file requirements without implying that every requested output can be supplied.

decisions.label: Describe the intended use
decisions.body: Ask where the photograph will appear and how it will be used so staff can explain the applicable reproduction and commercial-use terms. Keep availability, output and use in the same request. A reproduction fee should not be described as settling every permission or publication condition automatically.

ownerInputs: Current accession conventions and catalog-reference examples.
Available outputs and the approved LU limitation.
Reproduction, use-fee and staff-quote instructions.
sourceBridge: Waseca County Historical Society distinguishes reference web images from reproductions, asks for accession, location and size, and identifies an LU-prefix high-resolution limit.
limits: Staff determine availability, charges and use terms. A catalog match is not a file order or permission. Catalog, file-delivery and rights-management tools require separate assessment.

heading: Choose the meeting room alone or add exhibit access.
intro: An event-room rental can be arranged with or without a museum visit. Make that choice explicit, then show where food belongs and how the attendance estimate affects later charges.
customerQuestion: Does our event include the exhibits, and how will the final headcount be handled?

decisions.label: Name the rental option
